sentences.text: It is submitted that present is a case of false implication.

In the first leg of her submission before the Court, victim stated that her father and appellant-Satish Dhanak were consuming alcohol outside of her house and then there was an altercation between them, but, later on after being shown her previous videography, she changed her statement and said that on the relevant date,
Satish had given a 10 note to her sister and when her sister had gone away, he took off her clothes as well as his own and lay down over her.

It is submitted that even if the prosecution story is accepted in toto, then also present is a case of aggravated sexual assault as defined under Section 9(m) of POCSO Act and shall be punishable under Section 10 of the POCSO Act.

3. It is submitted that the evidence of lady doctor i.e. Dr.Meghana NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:26197 3 CRA-3215-2024 Pathak (PW-5) is relevant.
This witness had examined the victim on 18/01/2023 at District Hospital, Narsinghpur.
This witness deposed that mother of the victim had informed that Satish Dhanak had taken off his cloths and also that of the victim and in such condition he was caught hold of.
4. Shri Ajay Shukla, learned Public Prosecutor for the State, opposes the prayer and submits that victim (PW-1) has given a vivid description of the act.
5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

Dr. Meghana Pathak (PW-5), in para-4 of her examination-in-chief, categorically deposed that on external and internal examination,
there was no injury.
Hymen of the victim was intact.
There was no discharge or bleeding or any injury mark, therefore, she had not prepared any vaginal slide.
This witness also deposed that she had also not preserved her underwear because she was not wearing it at the time of her medical examination.
This witness has given categorical opinion that no sexual assault took place with the victim, at the most, its a case of attempt.
When these facts are taken into consideration, especially the evidence of victim, then present will be a case of aggravated sexual assault as defined under Section 9(m) of POCSO Act.
There is no medical evidence to substantiate the case except for the oral testimony of the victim and the DNA report is uninterpretable low.
In view of such facts, we hold that appellant, being guilty of aggravated assault, deserves to be convicted under Section 9(m)/10 of the POCSO Act.

Thus, the conviction of the appellant under Section 376 NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:26197 4 CRA-3215-2024 AB/511 of IPC is hereby altered to Section 9(m)/10 of POCSO Act.

Hence, impugned judgment dated 30/01/2024 passed by the learned 4th Additional Sessions Judge & Special Judge, POCSO Act, Narsinghpur (MP) in S.C.No.15/2023 is modified to the extent that instead of Section 376AB/511 of the IPC, the appellant is convicted under Section Satish Dhanak vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188436499/
2 9(m)/10 of POCSO Act and he is directed to undergo R.I. for five years along with fine of Rs.2,000/-
with a default stipulation to undergo additional R.I. for three months.
